security_audit.summary: Most static findings are expected for a shell-based Pexo API client and were dismissed where they are documentation-only, safely quoted helper commands, secure temp files, or masked diagnostics. Confirmed risks remain around credential transmission, local file upload to an external service, shell-sourced config, and prompt instruction priority claims.

remediation.issue: Prompt instructions claim highest priority over agent behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Remove highest-priority and non-negotiable wording. Present same-language behavior as a normal skill preference that remains subordinate to platform policy.

remediation.issue: Configuration files are sourced as shell code.
remediation.suggestion: Parse KEY=VALUE pairs without source, validate expected variable names, and recommend restrictive permissions on the config file.

remediation.issue: API keys are transmitted to the configured base URL.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the default base URL to trusted Pexo domains, warn before custom base URLs, and continue masking API keys in diagnostics.

remediation.issue: Local files can be uploaded to Pexo storage.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user intent before upload and reject hidden, config, or system paths unless the user specifically confirms them.

semantic_findings.title: Shell-Sourced Configuration File
semantic_findings.description: The shared helper sources the Pexo config file as shell code. A modified config file can execute arbitrary shell commands when any wrapper script loads it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files directly use source on the config path. This is a common convenience pattern, but it creates a real code execution risk if the config file is not trusted.

semantic_findings.title: Local File Upload To External Service
semantic_findings.description: The upload workflow accepts a local file path and sends that file to Pexo storage. This is required for media generation, but sensitive local files could be disclosed if the agent supplies the wrong path.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script obtains upload credentials and then uses curl --data-binary on the caller-provided path. The behavior is intentional and documented, so it is a privacy risk rather than hidden exfiltration.

content.value_statement: AI video production needs model selection, uploads, polling, and delivery steps. This skill guides agents through Pexo project creation, asset upload, chat, status polling, and final video delivery.
actual_capabilities: Creates Pexo projects using the included shell scripts.
Uploads supported image, video, and audio files to Pexo projects.
Sends user messages and asset tags to Pexo chat.
Polls project state and maps the next required action.
Retrieves preview and final video asset URLs.
Runs diagnostics for config, dependencies, network, and API key status.
limitations: Requires a Pexo account, API key, and reachable Pexo service.
Sends prompts and uploaded media to an external Pexo API.
Video generation depends on account credits and model availability.
Does not perform local video editing without Pexo generated assets.

use_cases.title: Create Product Ads
use_cases.description: Turn product photos, URLs, or short briefs into finished promotional videos.

use_cases.title: Produce Social Shorts
use_cases.description: Generate vertical clips for TikTok, Instagram Reels, or YouTube Shorts.

use_cases.title: Scale Catalog Videos
use_cases.description: Create repeated video assets from product media and consistent campaign instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Simple Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 15 second vertical video about my new product. Keep it clear, modern, and ready for social media.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Reference Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this uploaded product image as the main visual reference. Create a short product ad with clean lighting and a direct call to action.

prompt_templates.title: Revise a Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise the current video. Make the opening faster, keep the same product, and make the final message more direct.

prompt_templates.title: Build Campaign Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three short video variants from these assets. Use one calm brand version, one fast social version, and one product feature version.

output_examples.input: Create a 15 second product ad from this shoe photo.
output_examples.output: The request was submitted to Pexo with the uploaded image attached. The agent gives the project page, waits, then returns preview or final video links.

output_examples.input: The preview looks too slow. Make it faster and keep the same product.
output_examples.output: The revision feedback is sent to the same Pexo project. The agent resumes polling and reports the next preview or final delivery.

output_examples.input: Download the finished video for my project.
output_examples.output: The agent retrieves the final asset, downloads it to the local Pexo cache, and shares the full signed video URL.

best_practices: Confirm user intent before uploading local media to Pexo.
Run diagnostics before first use or after configuration errors.
Poll at 60 second intervals and avoid duplicate chat messages during WAIT.
anti_patterns: Do not upload unrelated local files or hidden configuration files.
Do not truncate signed video URLs when delivering final assets.
Do not send new chat messages while a project is still waiting.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Pexo account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires a Pexo API key and a configured Pexo base URL.

faq.question: Which agent tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What inputs can it use?
faq.answer: It can work with text, images, videos, audio, scripts, and URLs that are converted into uploaded files.

faq.question: Does it send data outside my machine?
faq.answer: Yes. It sends prompts and uploaded media to Pexo to generate videos.

faq.question: How are insufficient credits handled?
faq.answer: The scripts report credit errors and provide a Pexo top-up path when possible.

faq.question: What should I review before installing?
faq.answer: Review the shell scripts, external API use, API key handling, and local file upload behavior.
